Why AI visibility matters now: a growing share of people looking for a dance studio ask ChatGPT, Gemini, or Google's AI overview before they ever open a map. Studios that don't structure their site for those tools simply don't get mentioned — regardless of how good the studio actually is. In our checks, every studio the AI engines named was inside San Jose itself — none of the four studios in Los Gatos or Santa Clara came up.

Methodology: the field is every adult ballroom, Latin or partner-dance studio with a working website that appeared in Google's local results for San Jose dance searches on 14 Oct 2026. The Bay Area is split into five pages: San Francisco, Oakland (East Bay), San Jose (South Bay), Fremont (south Alameda County and the Tri-Valley) and San Mateo (the Peninsula). Areté Dance Center (Los Altos) and Feel Dance (Mountain View and Fremont) also show up in these searches; they're ranked on the San Mateo and Fremont pages. Each studio's site was crawled and graded across seven categories (AI readiness, SEO basics, page structure, content depth, social, image alt text, technical) on the same day. Google local positions come from four searches (ballroom dance lessons san jose ca, dance lessons san jose ca, salsa lessons san jose ca and wedding dance lessons san jose ca). AI visibility reflects live sessions in the public ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI apps, asked the two queries shown above; presence was confirmed by reading each engine's raw answer directly. This is an independent measurement by Ballroom Dance Directory, not commissioned by any studio named above. Rankings reflect a point-in-time snapshot and will be re-run periodically. The complete scorecard, Google table and AI answers are in the detailed report.

In San Jose, 15 studios compete for dance students. None has finished the work AI search now rewards.

We audited 15 dance and ballroom studios serving the San Jose market head to head: site quality, Google's local results, and 6 live checks across ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI. The sites range from 40 to 88. The AI engines name only eight of the 15, and all four studios in Los Gatos and Santa Clara were never named once. The field averages 66 (D) on AI readiness, 15 of 15 have no FAQ or Q&A structured data, and 8 of 15 have no llms.txt file. Whichever studio closes that gap first changes the answer for everyone searching this market.

Prepared by SiteTradeIn · Market snapshot generated 14 Oct 2026 · Independent audit — not commissioned by any studio in the field · See the ranked list

About this report

This is a market-wide snapshot, not an audit of a single business. We picked one competitive local market — dance and ballroom instruction in the San Jose, CA area — and ran the same measurement against every studio that competes for it: an automated site-quality grade across seven categories, where each studio shows up in Google's local results, and 6 live checks asking three AI engines who they'd recommend for two real buyer queries. Every studio named below is graded on identical criteria, on the same day, with no advance notice.

The point isn't to single any one studio out — it's to show what an AI-search-era competitive landscape actually looks like once you measure it instead of guessing at it. If your studio is one of the 15 below, this is where you stand today.

What the field shows

  • Artista Dance by Annaliza (88) and Arthur Murray Dance Studio Los Gatos (86) lead on site quality, and the field runs down to 40. Two scores are shared.
  • No studio earns an A for AI readiness. The field averages 66 (D) on the category that decides whether an AI engine can read, trust and quote a site; the best score in the market is 85.
  • None of the 15 studios has FAQ or Q&A structured data, and 8 have no llms.txt file — the two cheapest AI-answer signals available. No studio in the market has both.
  • Three of the 15 are franchise locations (two Arthur Murray and one Fred Astaire); the rest are independent studios.
  • The gap between #1 and #15 is 48 points on identical criteria. Nothing in the scorecard requires a rebuild or a rebrand to close it — just the work.

For a studio not doing this work, that's the default outcome — not a penalty, just the result of nobody in that seat having claimed it yet.

What separates the winners from the rest

  • Off-site proof, not just on-site polish. AI answers draw on what other sites say about a studio, not just on its own pages, so reviews, directory listings and a complete Google profile carry real weight.
  • Being unmistakably “in San Jose.” Every AI mention went to a studio inside the city. Studios that serve San Jose from nearby towns need pages, profiles and listings that say so in the words people search.
  • A complete, specific site. The strongest sites have no missing H1s or meta descriptions, alt text on their images, and schema that describes what the studio actually is.
  • Content matched to how people actually ask. The broad question and the ballroom question pull from different result sets — a studio needs to answer both.

Methodology & notes

Field (15 studios): artistadance.com, arthurmurraylosgatos.com, arthurmurraysanjose.com, sanjosebachatanights.com, thestarliteballroom.com, weevolvedance.com, parkavenueballroom.com, fredastaire.com/san-jose-valley-fair, mambonova.net, dna.dance, westvalleydanceco.com, danceboulevard.com, doyourownswing.com, volarestudios.net, studiomballroom.com. Chosen from live Google searches on 14 Oct 2026: every adult ballroom, Latin or partner-dance studio with a working website that appeared in Google's local results for San Jose dance searches. The Bay Area is split into five pages: San Francisco, Oakland (East Bay), San Jose (South Bay), Fremont (south Alameda County and the Tri-Valley) and San Mateo (the Peninsula). Areté Dance Center (Los Altos) and Feel Dance (Mountain View and Fremont) also show up in these searches; they're ranked on the San Mateo and Fremont pages. Left out: private instructors (Lesley McIntosh, Silicon Valley Ballroom's single instructor, Desiree May, Adam the Dancing Cowboy), MyWay Dance Studio (Linktree only), academia51 (no website), Silicon Valley Dance Club (its site is blank), San Jose Salsa Nights (its domain no longer resolves), clubs and dance events (Alberto's, For Dancers Only), hip-hop, K-pop and youth studios that lead the broad answers (On One, The Get Down, Purdance, How About Dance, Dancyn, South Bay Dance Center), and Ballroom Connection (a dancewear store).

Site audit: the same SiteTradeIn engine run for every studio on 14 Oct 2026, up to six pages per site, seven categories. Franchise locations that live on a national website (Fred Astaire) share that site's robots.txt, llms.txt, sitemap and templates.

AI visibility: 6 live checks — ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI, each asked “What are the best dance studios in San Jose, CA?” and “What are the best ballroom dance studios in San Jose, CA?” with a request for a top-five numbered list. Rankings are taken from each engine's own list; presence was confirmed by reading the raw response text, and every franchise mention was matched to its location. Each question was asked in a fresh session of each engine's public web app (ChatGPT and Gemini logged out, Google's AI Mode), not through a developer API.

Google: local (Places) and first-page organic results captured in a live browser session on 14 Oct 2026 for “ballroom dance lessons san jose ca”; “dance lessons san jose ca”; “salsa lessons san jose ca”; “wedding dance lessons san jose ca”; “ballroom dance lessons sunnyvale ca”, plus the organic searches “best dance studios in san jose ca” and “ballroom dance studio san jose”. Each query named the city; results vary by searcher location and over time.

Independence. This report is a market-wide measurement, not commissioned by or customized for any single studio named in it.

Limits. AI answers and search results vary between runs and over time; these are a point-in-time sample, not a fixed ranking.
